files.purpose: Zero-byte placeholder that reserves the .commandcode/taste/taste.md path in the repository so the Command Code CLI's per-repository 'taste' notes location exists and is tracked by git; it currently carries no guidance content at all (0 bytes, and its sha256 is the canonical empty-file hash e3b0c442...b7852b855).
platform_assumptions: Lives under a dot-directory (.commandcode) that is a Unix-style hidden folder; the Command Code CLI ('cmd', listed in README.md as a provider using headless print mode) owns .commandcode/ in the working tree.
feature_notes: File is completely empty: 0 bytes, 0 lines, no markdown heading, no front matter, no text.

Because .gitignore in this same bundle does not exclude .commandcode/, this empty file is committed deliberately to keep the directory present in checkouts (git does not track empty directories otherwise).

The Command Code provider is described in README.md as command `cmd`, 'headless print mode (NDJSON events), one run per turn, with a session mod for approvals'; this taste directory belongs to that CLI's own on-disk convention, not to Droppy Code's Swift sources.
unresolved_questions: Nothing in this bundle documents what the Command Code CLI writes into taste.md or when; the file is empty so its schema and format cannot be determined from it. The CommandCode provider sources under DroppyCode/Services/Providers would be needed to confirm whether Droppy Code itself reads or writes this path.
Cannot tell from this file alone whether it is read at runtime by the app or only by the external `cmd` binary.

files.purpose: Git ignore list for the Droppy Code Xcode project: excludes macOS Finder metadata, Xcode build and per-user state artifacts, an Xcode explicit-modules compiler-cache mishap directory, the generated website app captures, Cloudflare wrangler state and Python bytecode caches.
platform_assumptions: `.DS_Store` is a macOS Finder artifact.
`DerivedData/`, `xcuserdata/` and `*.xcuserstate` are Xcode-specific build and per-user UI state.

The inline comment says an Xcode explicit-modules build once wrote its compiler cache into DroppyCode.xcodeproj/-Xcc, so the `-Xcc/` pattern guards against a clang flag being taken as a directory name.
`build.noindex/` is the Spotlight-skipped release folder README.md names ('The disk image lands in build.noindex/, a folder Spotlight skips').
feature_notes: Exact 13 lines in order: `.DS_Store`, `build/`, `DerivedData/`, `xcuserdata/`, `*.xcuserstate`, `build.noindex/`, the comment `# An Xcode explicit-modules build once wrote its compiler cache into DroppyCode.xcodeproj/-Xcc.`, `-Xcc/`, a blank line, the comment `# The site's app captures are generated by scripts/website_captures.py and served from R2.`, `website/assets/app/`, `.wrangler/`, `__pycache__/`.
Names the generator script by path: scripts/website_captures.py produces website/assets/app/ captures which are served from Cloudflare R2, hence ignored here.

Notably does NOT ignore `.commandcode/`, `DroppyCode.xcodeproj/`, `.build/`, `Package.resolved` or `node_modules/`; the project is generated by xcodegen from project.yml per README.md yet the .xcodeproj is not ignored.
322 bytes over 13 lines, CRLF line terminators.
unresolved_questions: Whether DroppyCode.xcodeproj is committed or merely un-ignored cannot be confirmed from this file; README.md says `xcodegen generate` produces it, which would normally suggest ignoring it, so the absence of that rule is unexplained by this bundle.

files.purpose: The repository's working agreement for coding agents, titled '# AGENTS.md - DroppyCode agent workflow': mandatory git-worktree isolation, the four-layer source dependency rule, what a Hydra 'head' may and may not do, a hard ban on unprompted relaunches, the glab squash-merge policy, and the release-credits requirement.
calls_into: DroppyCode/App/HydraCookbook+Resolve.swift (cited as the example of splitting a Core file that needs the provider registry into an extension one layer up)
side_effects: Prescribes `git fetch origin --prune`, `git worktree add -b <branch> ~/.droppy-code/worktrees/agent-<slug> origin/main`, `git worktree remove --force ~/.droppy-code/worktrees/agent-<slug>` and `git worktree prune`.
Prescribes `xcodebuild -project DroppyCode.xcodeproj -scheme DroppyCode -configuration Debug build` as the only verification step.
Prescribes `glab mr create --squash-before-merge` and `glab mr merge --squash --remove-source-branch`.
Prescribes `python3 scripts/release_credits.py`, whose --check mode gates scripts/publish_release.sh.
platform_assumptions: Hardcoded macOS home path `/Users/jordyspruit/Desktop/DroppyCode` as the owner's checkout that must never be edited directly.
Worktree root `~/.droppy-code/worktrees/agent-<slug>` under the Unix home directory.
`xcodebuild` plus an Xcode project and scheme, i.e. a macOS-only toolchain.
`glab` (GitLab CLI) against a GitLab-hosted project, and `python3` on PATH.
ui_elements: States the app's About cards ignore the `### Thanks` heading, so adding Thanks changes nothing on Settings > About.
feature_notes: Exact worktree path template: `~/.droppy-code/worktrees/agent-<slug>`, branch created with `git worktree add -b <branch> ... origin/main` (or the agreed base branch).

Four-layer rule verbatim: DroppyCode/Core (models, pure support) reaches into nothing else; DroppyCode/Services (Git, Store, Providers) and DroppyCode/UI (Chrome, Common, Markdown, Theme, Sound) reach only into Core; DroppyCode/App (entry, model, runtime, windows, captures and every feature view) reaches into everything. New code goes in the lowest layer whose dependencies it has.
'There is no test target and no test scripts; the build is the check' - the upstream has no unit tests for the port to mirror.

Hydra head rule: 'A head never builds or otherwise verifies: no xcodebuild, no scripts/quick_run.sh, no check command.' It edits the files the lead briefed it on and reports, nothing more; the lead runs the one build that proves the change, in the checkout, after the heads report.

Relaunch ban is absolute: NEVER run scripts/quick_run.sh or otherwise quit/relaunch Droppy Code unless asked in that moment; building inside the worktree is fine, installing to /Applications and relaunching is not; 'Finish', 'merge', 'done' or 'test it' do not imply relaunch.

History facts stated: 4,292 commits on GitLab, mostly tiny Hydra head commits plus one merge commit per MR; the GitLab project's `merge_method` is `merge` and `squash_option` is `default_off`; every team merge MUST land as exactly one commit on main.
History rewriting (`rebase -i`, `filter-branch`, `filter-repo`, force-push to main) is forbidden; squash applies to new merges only. Never merge locally into main and never push straight to main.
Thanks bullet format is exact: `- Name (@gitlab-handle): what they did (!MR).`, placed after Refinements in every `## [x.y.z]` entry that ships outside work.
An outside merge request that lands between releases is added to `## [Unreleased]`'s Thanks right away rather than at release time.
unresolved_questions: scripts/quick_run.sh, scripts/release_credits.py and scripts/publish_release.sh are referenced but not in this bundle, so their exact flags beyond `--check` are unknown.
That quick_run.sh installs the built app to /Applications is implied by the relaunch rule's prose rather than confirmed by the script itself.

files.purpose: The machine-read release notes for Droppy Code: a Keep a Changelog v1.1.0 file whose `## [<version>] - <date>` sections are published verbatim as GitLab release notes and rendered as the app's Settings > About New features / Bug fixes / Refinements cards. Covers 1.0.0 (2026-09-13) through 1.6.0 (2026-09-18) plus an Unreleased section, and is the richest behavioral specification in the repository root.
calls_into: scripts/publish_release.sh (reads the section matching the version in project.yml)
scripts/build_changelog.py (builds website/changelog.json from the same sections)
side_effects: Both publish_release.sh and build_changelog.py read this file and skip `## [Unreleased]`; the next release renames that heading to its version and date.
Publishing stops until every outside contributor is named in a `### Thanks` block.
platform_assumptions: Every release headline states 'Apple silicon, macOS 26 or later. Signed and notarized.'

The Unreleased bug fix describes macOS 27 behavior: a popover's window coming on screen can make the framework's remote view throw from inside the notification that announces it, and because that happens during a SwiftUI layout pass AppKit catches the exception and stops the app; both reports came on September 18 from the release-notes cards on Settings > About.
AppKit and SwiftUI specifics recur: the window drag region computed mid layout pass, title-bar layout, traffic lights, popovers, key view loop owned by AppKit, Liquid Glass materials.
ui_elements: Settings > About cards titled 'New features', 'Bug fixes' and 'Refinements'; the Unreleased change opens their section in a card under the row instead of in a popover, folded away by tapping the card again or its close button.

Settings > General > Projects: a project mark, either an emoji or an SF Symbol; the activity list can draw that mark in front of a thread's name in place of the line that named the project, one line per thread, with what the thread is doing still at the end of the row. The list choice sits on the General page and on the welcome screen, and a new install starts on the compact one.

Usage-limit notice with two buttons: 'Cancel' stops the automatic continue and leaves the chat to you; 'New thread' stops the wait and opens a new chat of the same project holding a hand-off of the request and of what the stopped turn had already done.
Settings > Hydra > Heads: 'Auto-hide heads in the sidebar', off by default.
Settings > Hydra 'Heads at once' row of buttons: Off or 1 to 8, off by default; the uncapped choice is drawn as an infinity sign and reads as 'No cap' to VoiceOver.
Codex usage panel plan wording: account type `pro` reads 'Pro 20x' (was 'Pro'), `prolite` reads 'Pro 5x' (was 'Prolite'), and `self_serve_business_prolite` reads 'Business Premium'.
Settings > Conversation: the 'Chronological order' switch (added in 1.5.5, removed in Unreleased) and 'Show activity while working'.
The 'Worked for ...' fold line on a finished turn, with the turn's steps, its heads and its changed-files card behind it.
Banked resets row reads 'Banked resets - 2 available' on one line with the outcome of a spend below it.
Claude resume warning text: 'Claude no longer has this conversation. It starts a new one here'.
GitLab MCP failure text: 'gitlab.com didn't answer its MCP address (404), try again in a few minutes'.
Effort slider whose knob is a Liquid Glass lens; it fuses the lead's and the heads' colours for a pair.
Hydra heads' panel picker options named 'One panel' and 'A panel each'.

Keyboard: Command-W asks to archive the thread (Return archives, Escape keeps it, Delete sits beside Archive), Command-S settles it, Command-B shows and hides the sidebar, Command-1 to Command-9 switch to the first nine threads before the menu bar sees the chord, Escape stops a running turn and takes it back or dismisses whatever is in front while a field being typed in keeps its Escape.
feature_notes: Format contract in the header: 'The format follows Keep a Changelog (https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/); versions are the release tags without the `v`', with the heading example `## [1.5.4] - 2026-09-17`.

1.6.0 scope line: folds a finished turn into its 'Worked for ...' line with the turn's steps behind the chevron, keeps a running turn's steps and the agent's thinking in the card below its bar, hands a chat stopped by its provider's usage limit a New thread that carries the work on, lets the heads leave the sidebar on their own, and puts a mark of your choosing in front of a project's name; Netlify joins the MCP catalog.
Netlify MCP connector: sign in with a Netlify account and a thread can create projects, deploy sites and manage environment variables.

GitLab MCP: a top-level group that has not allowed MCP client access is answered by GitLab 19.4 and earlier with 404 instead of 'MCP server disabled'; the app's own MCP proxy now answers a path it has no route for with 502 rather than a 404 that reads as the server's reply.
Escape on a running turn stops it and takes it back: the conversation and the provider's context rewind to before it and the message returns to the chat box; files stay as the turn left them.
Hydra head concurrency: at most eight run at a time with the rest queued, heads pace their flushes by how many are streaming, and twenty heads out at once used to freeze the app.
Head progress bars cache their staves between frames instead of walking every step of the timeline thirty times a second; three hangs of six seconds each came from that walk.
A thread opens on its last three blocks so switching to a long chat paints at once; the chat columns either side of the selected thread stay built.
Long threads run at 120 fps: rows laid out as they come into view, blocks cached, streamed chunks coalesced off the main thread.
Attachment files no thread refers to any more are swept from disk a day after they were written.
API keys live in the Keychain alone: the copy the defaults held in plain text is gone, and old copies are cleared at launch.
With 'Heads work at a working effort' on, a lead at Max on a model whose scale has no medium (Z.ai's GLM) sends its heads out at the scale's middle rung.

Themes: 26 tinted-glass themes from System to Catppuccin, Dracula, Tokyo Night, Nord, Gruvbog, Solarized, GitHub, Matrix and Claude/Codex, plus a window transparency setting (spelling of Gruvbox in the file is 'Gruvbox').

Welcome tour: six pages of real captures at 1.2.0, eight pages of new captures over the desktop at 1.3.0 including the floating thread list and Hydra's cookbook; Help > Welcome tour and About open it again.
Banked resets: Codex at 1.3.0, Z.ai at 1.4.0 for the 5-hour and the weekly limit each with its expiry, spent after a confirm step so the limit goes back to zero.
A Debug build runs as 'Droppy Code Dev' beside the release app, with its own library and settings.

Provider arrivals: 1.0.0 Codex, Claude, Cursor, OpenCode, Grok, DeepSeek, Meta, Devin and Antigravity; 1.1.0 GitHub Copilot CLI with its models, efforts and monthly quotas; 1.2.0 Command Code with approvals, plan limits and remaining credits; 1.3.0 Pi with supervised, auto-accept and full-access approval levels, and Z.ai with the GLM Coding Plan.
1.3.0 records 'The license is GNU AGPL v3 with attribution'; 1.1.1 added Settings > About > Licenses shipping the app's license, third-party notices and trademark policy inside the app.
1.5.4 refinement records the four-layer source reorganisation: 'The source is arranged in four layers, Core, Services, UI and App, so a change to a model, a provider or a view has one home.'

The merge card in the timeline walks a track of dots, one per stage, that fills as the merge moves through its stages, with the head hopping along above it and a small bounce once every dot lights; finished heads and the merge pill settle with a glide transition.
1.5.6 fix: a session's ID now reaches the chat with its first message, and a session replaced before then is followed by one that starts fresh with no resume attempt and no warning.

1.6.0 Thanks names three outside contributors with exact MR numbers: Rene (@diazdesandi) !307 and !308; Bryan Galdamez (@JosueGalRe) !283, !285, !304, !306; Nikita Tsyganov (@nik1tsyganov) !293. 1.5.0 credits nik1tsyganov inline for the per-project Hydra pair rule.

!307 names concrete symbols: `search_text` confined to the project root with a `--` guard against flag smuggling, plan mode blocking edits after approve-for-turn, clearing the save timer handle before `saveNow` bails, and `WorkingTreeWatch` not tearing down the registered watch when a second caller lost the race. !308 put one OpenAI-compatible session and one Keychain behind the DeepSeek, Meta and Z.ai providers.

OpenCode reports the reasoning levels of the model a session is on, so the catalog asks it for each model in turn, the way it already did for Cursor; a model catalog probe that came back empty is retried on the next ask (!306).
Claude lost-session handling: 'No conversation found with session ID' plus a CLI that exits before answering the first request is treated as a lost session and a new one begins.

Per-project Hydra pair: right-click a project in the sidebar to choose the pair each of its new chats starts on; 'The chat's last pair' removes the rule, and a pair removed from Settings takes its project rules with it.

1.5.5 head profiles: purpose-named configurations ('quick', 'deep', 'visual' or any word) with their own provider, model or effort, edited in the pair's Head profiles section in Settings; the lead hears which profiles exist and routes each task to one by name in its delegation block, and a task without a profile, or with a name the pair does not have, runs on the heads' shared model.

1.2.0 Hydra floating panels: the team's panel and any head popped out of it float over the chat, dock in any corner, stack when they share one, and can be dragged to size; a finished head wears its outcome on its glyph and every head has its own progress bar with its task and time.

1.5.1 merge scoping: each chat's merge carries only its own team's work; when a chat's work already sits on main Hydra says so and marks the heads merged; when the team's files lie outside the chat's project Hydra names the project they belong to and asks you to open the chat there.
unresolved_questions: The Unreleased section is undated and unversioned, so the next version number the port should target is not stated here; project.yml, not in this bundle, holds the version.
The prose describes behavior but not the numeric constants behind it (animation durations, panel sizes, the popover height cap named in 1.5.3); those must come from the Swift sources.
scripts/build_changelog.py and website/changelog.json are named but not in this bundle, so the JSON schema the site consumes is unknown.

files.asset_inspection: bundle.mjs printed 'binary' in its line column for this path, but the file is plain ASCII text with CRLF line terminators, 37,215 bytes, 684 lines (verified with `file` and `wc -l`), so it was read end to end as text rather than inspected as an asset. No binary content is present.
files.purpose: The project's licence file: a 22-line Droppy Code header that places the work under GNU AGPL v3 with three named section 7 additional terms (attribution, origin, names and marks) and a portions-under-other-licenses paragraph for T3 Code, followed by the verbatim GNU Affero General Public License Version 3, 19 November 2007 text.
key_symbols: ADDITIONAL TERMS UNDER SECTION 7 OF THE GNU AFFERO GENERAL PUBLIC LICENSE
GNU AFFERO GENERAL PUBLIC LICENSE Version 3, 19 November 2007
Preamble; TERMS AND CONDITIONS sections 0 through 17; END OF TERMS AND CONDITIONS; How to Apply These Terms to Your New Programs
ui_elements: Term (a) requires the attribution string in an 'About screen or equivalent user-visible credits', which is the app's Settings > About > Licenses page added in 1.1.1 per CHANGELOG.md.
feature_notes: Copyright lines: 'Droppy Code' then 'Copyright (c) 2026 Jordy Spruit (Droppy)'.
Licensed under the AGPL 'version 3 of the License' only, with no 'or any later version' clause.

Term (a) attribution is the binding string for the port, verbatim: 'Droppy Code by Jordy Spruit (Droppy), https://getdroppycode.app', required in the About screen or equivalent user-visible credits, in the README or equivalent documentation, and in the copyright notices of its source files; THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md must be preserved.
Term (b) origin: modified versions must be marked as modified and must not be presented as the original Droppy Code or as endorsed by, made by or affiliated with Droppy or Jordy Spruit.

Term (c) names and marks: the licence grants no rights to use the names 'Droppy' or 'Droppy Code', the Droppy Code icon or any other Droppy mark, except as required to preserve the attribution; it points at TRADEMARK.md.

PORTIONS UNDER OTHER LICENSES: Droppy Code began as a native Swift rewrite of T3 Code, Copyright (c) 2026 T3 Tools Inc., released under the MIT License; that notice is preserved in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md and continues to apply to the portions that descend from it, alongside this License for the work as a whole.

A 72-hyphen rule line separates the project header from the FSF text; the FSF body is the unmodified 2007 AGPL (Preamble, sections 0 to 17, END OF TERMS AND CONDITIONS, How to Apply These Terms to Your New Programs).
AGPL section 13 (Remote Network Interaction; Use with the GNU General Public License) is present unmodified, which is what obliges a network-served modified version to offer its Corresponding Source.

The 'How to Apply These Terms' boilerplate is the stock FSF template with placeholders `<one line to give the program's name and a brief idea of what it does.>` and `Copyright (C) <year>  <name of author>`; it is not filled in for Droppy Code.
Section 8 reinstatement windows are the standard 60 days and 30 days; section 11's discriminatory-patent-license cutoff is 28 March 2007.
unresolved_questions: Why bundle.mjs classified this file as binary is not determinable from the file itself; `file` reports ASCII text with very long lines (391) and CRLF terminators, so the classifier likely keys on long lines or CRLF rather than on real binary content.

files.purpose: The project's front page and the best top-level map of the app: an HTML header image, the provider/CLI/protocol table, the feature list, the macOS requirements, the xcodegen build steps, the release and publish scripts, the four-layer source layout table, acknowledgements, and the licence, credit and contributor asks.
key_symbols: Provider table (Provider | Command line tool | Protocol)
calls_into: docs/icon.png (header image, HTML width=128, alt 'Droppy Code icon')
docs/droppy-logo.png (Made by Droppy image, HTML width=64, alt 'Droppy logo')
side_effects: Build steps: `brew install xcodegen`, `xcodegen generate`, `open DroppyCode.xcodeproj`.
scripts/release.sh archives an Apple silicon build, signs it with Developer ID, notarizes and staples both the app and a disk image, and checks Gatekeeper; the disk image lands in build.noindex/.
scripts/package_dmg.sh gives the disk image a styled drag-to-Applications window; its background and baked window layout live in release/dmg and the volume icon is the app's own.

scripts/publish_release.sh tags the version from project.yml, creates the GitLab release with the notes from the `## [<version>]` section of CHANGELOG.md, and points the latest-download permalink at the new disk image, which is what Settings > About and the website's download button resolve to.
platform_assumptions: 'A native macOS app for your coding agents. Written entirely in Swift and SwiftUI with Liquid Glass, for Macs with Apple silicon on macOS 26 and later.'
Requirements: a Mac with Apple silicon running macOS 26 or later; at least one provider installed and signed in; Git, plus `gh` or `glab` for pull requests.
Homebrew for xcodegen, an Xcode project, and Swift Package Manager fetching SwiftTerm (Xcode asks once to trust its build plugin).
Developer ID signing, notarization, stapling and Gatekeeper checks are Apple-only release steps; build.noindex/ is a Spotlight-skipped folder name.
persisted_fields: `droppy-code.json` is named as the per-project file carrying project scripts.
Native-API providers are keyed by environment variables: `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` (DeepSeek), `ZAI_API_KEY` (Z.ai), `MODEL_API_KEY` (Meta, at `api.meta.ai/v1`, Muse Spark).
ui_elements: Projects and threads in a glass sidebar with search, pinning, settling (or archiving), and drag to resize; a settled thread drops to the bottom, small and grey, until you reopen it.
Streaming conversations with reasoning, tool calls, plans, to-do lists and errors; approvals and questions from the agent answered inline.
Plan mode, model and reasoning selection, and four permission modes per thread.
Twenty-six tinted-glass themes, from System to Catppuccin, Dracula, Claude and Codex.
A diff for every turn captured as hidden git checkpoints, with revert; an embedded terminal per thread plus project scripts from droppy-code.json; new threads in their own git worktree.
Commit, push and pull requests with generated commit messages and thread titles; a command palette, keyboard shortcuts and notifications when work finishes.
A welcome tour on first launch, six pages of real captures; the Help menu opens it again.

The usage ring beside the send button opens a popover with the context window, each plan's rolling limits and resets (Codex, Claude, Antigravity, Copilot, Command Code and Z.ai) and the credit left on DeepSeek and Command Code keys; a pair across two providers stacks the lead's over the heads'. A switch in General settings keeps the same in a floating panel beside the chat, and Settings > Providers shows every signed-in account at once. A Codex account that has banked resets can spend one from the same popover to clear its active windows.
feature_notes: Provider table exactly as written: Codex -> `codex` -> app-server JSON-RPC; Claude -> `claude` -> stream-json with permission prompts; Cursor -> `cursor-agent` -> Agent Client Protocol; OpenCode -> `opencode` -> Agent Client Protocol; Grok -> `grok` -> Agent Client Protocol; Antigravity -> `agy` -> stream-json headless; Copilot -> `copilot` -> headless JSON-RPC (the Copilot SDK protocol); Command Code -> `cmd` -> headless print mode (NDJSON events), one run per turn, with a session mod for approvals; Pi -> `pi` -> RPC mode (JSONL over stdio), one process per thread, with a gate extension for approvals; DeepSeek -> `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` -> native API (OpenAI-compatible); Z.ai -> `ZAI_API_KEY` -> native API (OpenAI-compatible, GLM Coding Plan); Meta -> `MODEL_API_KEY` -> native API at `api.meta.ai/v1` (Muse Spark).

Hydra: one chat, many heads. Switch it on and the agent leads a team of helper agents on big jobs: it writes the briefs, sends the heads out in parallel, each in its own copy of the project, and their work lands back in your checkout as one merge. Each head has a floating panel, and a pair sets the lead's model and the heads' model; a pair can cross providers, a strong lead on one and quick heads on another, with one effort slider fused for both.
Explicit non-goals, verbatim: 'Remote access, mobile apps, cloud sync, telemetry and a web client are left out on purpose.'
Login examples given: `codex login`, `claude auth login`, `copilot login`, `cmd login` or `pi` (then `/login`).
SwiftTerm is stated as the only dependency, fetched by Swift Package Manager.

Layout table: DroppyCode/Core holds models and pure support - projects and threads, timelines, providers (`ProviderKind` lives here), Hydra, shortcuts, process I/O, JSON-RPC and the login shell - and depends on nothing else in the app. DroppyCode/Services holds Git, worktrees and diff parsing, the on-disk store, and the Codex, Claude, ACP, Antigravity, Copilot, Command Code, Pi, DeepSeek, Meta and Z.ai adapters behind one event model; depends on Core. DroppyCode/UI holds window chrome, common controls, Markdown rendering, the theme and the chimes; depends on Core only. DroppyCode/App holds the app entry, commands and settings, the project library, the per-thread runtime, windows, captures and every feature view: sidebar, chat, composer, changes, terminal, palette, settings, usage and the tour. `website` is the marketing site, a static page published by Netlify via netlify.toml.

Acknowledgements name the exact ported pieces: T3 Code by T3 Tools Inc. (MIT) as the Swift rewrite's origin, in T3 Code's own repository so this repo's history carries their work; SwiftTerm by Miguel de Icaza (MIT) as the terminal; the working indicators, the gradient pulse beside a reply and the mini pulse on working threads with their rotating words ported from Zeron by Wing (MIT); spending a Codex account's banked resets from the usage popover following MonoCode by hardbeat920 (MIT); the Copilot provider icon being the `copilot` mark from GitHub's Octicons (MIT). The app carries the same notices under Settings > About > Licenses.

License paragraph: GNU AGPL v3.0 with additional attribution terms; anyone who distributes it or a modified version, or runs a modified version for others over a network, must make their source available under the same license and keep the credit to Droppy Code by Jordy Spruit (Droppy); modified versions must say they are modified and must not present themselves as Droppy Code; the names 'Droppy' and 'Droppy Code' and their icons are not part of the license.

Credit ask, verbatim: keep the line 'Droppy Code by Jordy Spruit (Droppy), https://getdroppycode.app' in your About screen, your README and your source headers, and keep THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md. 'That is the whole ask.'

Contributors policy: every release names the people whose merge requests shipped in it, in the Thanks section of the release entry in CHANGELOG.md, the GitLab release notes and the changelog page on getdroppycode.app; a merge request that lands is credited under the author's name and GitLab handle in the next release.
unresolved_questions: The provider table omits Devin, which CHANGELOG.md 1.0.0 and THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md both list as a provider, so whether Devin still ships, or ships without a CLI/protocol row, cannot be settled from this bundle.
The feature list says the welcome tour has six pages while CHANGELOG.md 1.3.0 says eight pages of new captures; the README may be stale on that number.
docs/icon.png and docs/droppy-logo.png are referenced but not in this bundle, so their pixel dimensions are unknown; only the HTML display widths 128 and 64 are stated.

files.purpose: The attribution file that LICENSE term (a) requires to be preserved: nine sections (Droppy Code, T3 Code, Synara, SwiftTerm, MonoCode, Zeron, Octicons, TourKit, Provider names and marks), each naming the exact upstream file or files that were ported or studied and reproducing the MIT licence text. It is also shipped inside the app under Settings > About > Licenses.
platform_assumptions: SwiftTerm is fetched by Swift Package Manager and linked into the app, a macOS Swift toolchain assumption.

Zeron's ported sources are an iOS SwiftUI app (apps/ios/Zeron/Views/Loaders.swift and apps/ios/Zeron/Theme/Motion.swift), so the working indicators are SwiftUI animation code carried from iOS to macOS.
TourKit is a macOS slideshow with a floating window controller, ported to the app's glass and asset catalog.

SwiftTerm carries a four-line copyright stack: Miguel de Icaza 2019-2026, the xterm.js authors 2017-2019, SourceLair Private Company 2014-2016, Christopher Jeffrey 2012-2013.

Synara is explicitly architecture-only, 'a TypeScript app whose architecture was read, not copied', and its studied principles are the app's performance contract: nothing synchronous on the click that opens a chat (its history decodes off the main thread and the selection paints first), one write to the library for a click rather than one per thread, timeline blocks kept per thread across switches so coming back to a chat reuses them, the chat column staying put while only the transcript is swapped, sidebar rows reading their own thread rather than the whole list, generous parse caches so scrolling back through a long thread never parses again, and rows built lazily so a popover opens on what is visible. 'No Synara code is in this repository.'

MonoCode's ported behavior is specified exactly: the app-server's `account/rateLimitResetCredit/consume` call sent with an idempotency key, the reset credits read beside the rate limits, the confirm step before a reset is spent, and the four outcomes it can answer with; the cited upstream files are src/lib/rateLimitsFetch.ts and src/chrome/UsageProviderChip.tsx. 'No MonoCode code is in this repository.'
Octicons: the icon is the `copilot` mark from icons/copilot-24.svg with its artboard resized to match the other provider marks.

Provider names and marks disclaimer lists Codex, Claude, Cursor, OpenCode, Grok, DeepSeek, Meta, Devin, Antigravity, GitHub Copilot and Command Code as the names and marks of their respective owners, used to name the agents the app drives, and states Droppy Code is not affiliated with or endorsed by any of them.

files.purpose: The trademark policy that LICENSE term (c) points to: it declares 'Droppy', 'Droppy Code', the Droppy logo (the water droplet) and the Droppy Code icon as trademarks of Jordy Spruit held back from the AGPL grant, and lists what a fork may and may not do with the names and branding.
feature_notes: Marks named exactly: 'Droppy', 'Droppy Code', the Droppy logo (the water droplet) and the Droppy Code icon, trademarks of Jordy Spruit, all rights reserved.
The source code is available under the GNU AGPL v3.0 with additional attribution terms, but the names and the associated branding are protected and are not licensed with the code.

You MAY: refer to this project as 'Droppy Code' when discussing or reviewing it; use the names in factual statements (e.g., 'based on Droppy Code'); fork the code for personal use or contribution back to this project.

You MAY NOT: distribute a modified version under the names 'Droppy' or 'Droppy Code'; use 'Droppy', 'Droppy Code' or similar names (Droppie, DroppyCoder, etc.) for derivative products; use the Droppy logo or the Droppy Code icon in your own projects; imply official endorsement or affiliation without permission.

Fork checklist, four numbered steps: 1. Choose a distinctly different name; 2. Create your own branding and icons; 3. Remove all Droppy trademarks from your distribution; 4. Clearly indicate your project is not affiliated with Droppy.
Attribution examples use emoji marks: '"Based on Droppy Code" or "Forked from Droppy Code"' with a white heavy check mark, versus '"Droppy Code 2.0" or "Droppy Code Pro"' with a cross mark.

Contact for trademark licensing inquiries or permissions: Email hi@getdroppy.app, Website https://getdroppy.app - note this is getdroppy.app, the parent brand, not the app's own getdroppycode.app used in the attribution string.
unresolved_questions: The policy forbids using the Droppy Code icon while LICENSE term (a) requires preserving the attribution string in a user-visible About credit; how a fork should render that credit without any mark is left to the porter, and no substitute wordmark or icon-free credit layout is specified here.

files.purpose: Netlify deployment configuration for the getdroppycode.app marketing site: publishes the website/ folder with no build step, and defines four redirects (including the /download/latest permalink every download button on the page resolves to) plus three header blocks for security and caching.
calls_into: scripts/publish_release.sh (keeps the GitLab latest-release permalink pointing at Droppy-Code.dmg)
side_effects: Deploy command documented in the header comment: `netlify deploy --prod --dir website` from the repository root so this file's redirects and headers ride along.
platform_assumptions: Hosted on Netlify; the release artifact is a macOS disk image named Droppy-Code.dmg hosted on GitLab releases.
ui_elements: 'The download button everywhere on the page points here' - the site's download button targets /download/latest.
feature_notes: [build] publish = "website"; static, no build step, Netlify publishes the folder as-is.

Redirect 1: from "/download/latest" to "https://gitlab.com/droppyformac1/droppy-code/-/releases/permalink/latest/downloads/Droppy-Code.dmg", status 302, force = true. The comment explains GitLab's permalink resolves to the newest release's disk image because every release links its image as /Droppy-Code.dmg (scripts/publish_release.sh sees to that), so a new release changes nothing here or in the HTML.
Redirect 2: from "https://www.getdroppycode.app/*" to "https://getdroppycode.app/:splat", status 301, force = true; www is an alias and this also covers a deploy preview that reaches the rule first.
Redirect 3: from "/download" to "/download/latest", status 301, no force.
Redirect 4: from "/releases" to "https://gitlab.com/droppyformac1/droppy-code/-/releases", status 302, no force.
Headers for "/*": X-Content-Type-Options = "nosniff", X-Frame-Options = "DENY", Referrer-Policy = "strict-origin-when-cross-origin", Permissions-Policy = "camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=()".
Headers for "/assets/*": Cache-Control = "public, max-age=604800", one week; the comment notes CSS/JS carry ?v= for instant busting.
Headers for "/*.html": Cache-Control = "public, max-age=0, must-revalidate"; the HTML must not be cached.
Reveals the GitLab namespace: gitlab.com/droppyformac1/droppy-code.
unresolved_questions: No Content-Security-Policy or Strict-Transport-Security header is set here; whether those are configured elsewhere (the Netlify UI or a _headers file inside website/) cannot be determined from this bundle.
The website/ directory is not in this bundle, so which pages sit behind these redirects, for example a changelog page built from website/changelog.json, is not verifiable here.
